lyrics:
[Intro: fingerpicked banjo, soft kick drum]

[Verse 1: plain raw male voice]
Town I'm from's got one red light
It blinks. It doesn't even change.
Nobody famous ever left here
Nobody's ever heard my name

I stock shelves on the late shift
Talk to the radio driving home
Seven billion people out there
I figured I was on my own

[Chorus: stomps, gang vocals, wide open]
I'm a nobody from nowhere
And you know my middle name
You count the hairs, you catch the tears
You've been here every day
Maker of the Milky Way
Asking how my shift went
A nobody from nowhere
And you call me your friend

[Verse 2: voice closer, banjo and bass]
You picked a town like this one once
People said nothing good came out
Worked with your hands for thirty years
Nobody wrote it down

A nobody from Nazareth
Hung on a hill between two thieves
Turns out the King of everything
Knows what it's like to be me

[Chorus: stomps, gang vocals, wide open]
I'm a nobody from nowhere
And you know my middle name
You count the hairs, you catch the tears
You've been here every day
Maker of the Milky Way
Asking how my shift went
A nobody from nowhere
And you call me your friend

[Bridge: band drops, voice and banjo, then a swell]
I didn't climb up. I couldn't have.
I never even left this place.
You came all the way down here.
That's grace. That's grace.

[Final Chorus: full band, everyone shouting]
I'm a nobody from nowhere
And you know my middle name
You count the hairs, you catch the tears
You've been here every day
Maker of the Milky Way
Asking how my shift went
A nobody from nowhere
And Jesus calls me friend

[Outro: banjo, a truck door, radio static]
